config: single OVS switch multi-homed to all 3 ONOS controllers (tcp:172.20.0.5/6/7:6653)
method: docker kill (SIGKILL) the current ONOS master; poll REST device-mastership on a surviving node until mastership moves to a live node; restart killed node and wait for 3-node READY between trials
caveats: CONTROL-plane mastership failover: time from SIGKILL of the master to a surviving controller taking mastership of a multi-homed switch; bounded by the Atomix failure-detection/term timeout.

Requires the switch to be multi-homed (connected to all 3 controllers). The pilot fabric shards each switch to ONE controller, which gives NO OF-layer failover (killing that controller disconnects the switch); the resilient design multi-homes, which is what is measured here.

Data-plane forwarding from already-installed flow rules persists through the window (OpenFlow fail-static, E10); device_stayed_available confirms the switch never lost connectivity (still attached to 2 survivors).
Single switch, single EC2 host, container-local cluster; wall-clock indicative, not a datacenter-grade bound.
